behavior_items: The bug report describes a Fortran derived type whose components have default initialization specified in the type definition, including integer fields initialized to values such as -1 and 0 and logical fields initialized to .true. or .false..

The reproducer exercises two code paths for the same derived type state: a direct local declaration like `type(t_test) :: x`, and creation of a value through a function returning `type(t_test)` as its result.

The expected language behavior is that every object of the derived type begins with all default-initialized components set from the type declaration, regardless of whether the object is declared directly or appears as a function result.

The observed behavior before invoking the constructor/function path shows correct default initialization: integer components print as the declared values and logical components also match their defaults.

The failing behavior occurs after constructing or receiving the object through a function result: some integer components contain garbage values instead of their declared defaults, while the logical components still appear correct in the printed output.

This indicates that the compiler path handling function result creation for a derived type with default-initialized components is not performing full default initialization of the result object before use or before partial assignment.

Because only some fields become corrupted while others retain expected values, the exercised path likely copies or assigns only explicitly set parts of the result, leaving other scalar storage uninitialized.
The reproducer therefore distinguishes between ordinary object declaration semantics and function-result materialization semantics, demonstrating that gfortran mishandles the latter.

The mention that Intel Fortran produces the expected values in both cases strengthens the interpretation that the source is valid and that GCC/gfortran is failing to honor default component initialization for function results.

The report also notes the same behavior in gfortran 11, suggesting the issue is not tied to a single release but to a longer-standing implementation bug in derived-type result construction or return-value lowering.

The compiler behavior exercised is specifically the generation of code for a function returning a nontrivial derived type with default-initialized components, followed by printing the returned object's fields to reveal whether initialization actually occurred.

The wrong values shown for integer members are characteristic of reading uninitialized stack or temporary storage, implying the returned temporary/result variable is allocated but not fully initialized from the type defaults.
test_behavior_analysis.summary: The reproducer targets gfortran's handling of Fortran derived types with default component initialization when such a type is produced as a function result. A directly declared object of the type is initialized correctly, proving the type definition itself is valid. But when the same type is returned from a function/constructor path, some components—especially integers—contain garbage instead of their declared defaults, while others may coincidentally remain correct. This demonstrates a compiler bug in result-object construction or return lowering: gfortran is not applying the type's default initialization semantics consistently for function results.

test_failure_analysis.analysis: The failure pattern is consistent with a gfortran bug in the function-result creation path for Fortran derived types that have default component initialization. A directly declared object of the type is initialized correctly, so the type metadata and ordinary declaration-time initialization logic are working. The corruption appears only when an object is produced as a function result, which isolates the defect to result-variable materialization, temporary creation, or return-value lowering rather than to the source program. The fact that integer fields become garbage while logical fields may still print expected values suggests the compiler is not performing full default initialization on the hidden result object, or is only copying explicitly assigned components and leaving the rest of the storage uninitialized. This points to a missing or incomplete call to the default-initialization machinery for derived-type function results, possibly in code paths for structure constructors, intrinsic assignment to the result, or generation of temporaries used to return derived values.
possible_causes: Missing default component initialization when lowering or expanding a function result variable of derived type in gfortran.
Incorrect code generation for derived-type return temporaries: the hidden result object is allocated/copied without first applying type default initializers.
Partial component-wise assignment into the function result that copies only explicitly set fields and fails to initialize untouched components from the type definition.
Front-end semantic handling of structure constructor or function-result entities does not mark the result as requiring default initialization, unlike normal local declarations.
Bug in derived-type assignment/copy construction for returned values where uninitialized padding or scalar members are propagated because initialization is skipped before assignment.
Special-case path for module procedures or returned nontrivial derived types bypasses the normal initialization tree/code used for local variables with default-initialized components.
evidence: The same derived type is correctly initialized when declared locally, proving ordinary declaration semantics work and the source type definition is valid.
The failure appears only after obtaining the object through a function result, isolating the problem to function-result handling rather than general derived-type initialization.
Garbage integer values are characteristic of uninitialized stack or temporary storage, matching a missed initialization step in the returned-result object.
Only some components are wrong while others remain correct, which is consistent with partial assignment/copying instead of full default initialization.
Intel Fortran produces the expected values for both paths, supporting that the reproducer is valid and GCC is mishandling standard-conforming semantics.
The bug is reported across multiple gfortran versions, indicating a persistent implementation issue in derived-type result construction/return lowering rather than a transient regression.

selected_files.reason: Most suspicious because the bug is in gfortran’s lowering of a function returning a derived type with default-initialized components. The failure pattern strongly suggests the function-result/temporary construction path does not apply full default initialization before partial assignment or return copying, and trans-expr.cc is the main expression translation file for such result materialization and structure-constructor-like expression handling.

Highly relevant because default initialization for ordinary local derived-type objects works, so the missing step may be in how backend decls are created for hidden function result variables or temporaries. trans-decl.cc handles backend function and variable declarations and is a likely place where result variables should be marked or expanded with default initialization semantics.

Likely involved as shared Fortran translation infrastructure for creating temporaries and lowering executable constructs. If the special function-result path bypasses the normal initialization sequence used for local declarations, the bug could be in generic translation support here rather than only in expression-specific code.

Possible frontend source of the problem if structure constructor or function-result expressions are represented without preserving the need for default component initialization of omitted fields. The observed partial initialization behavior is consistent with frontend expression construction that only carries explicit component values forward.

Less likely than translation files, but still plausible if semantic resolution of function results or derived-type constructors fails to mark that default-initialized components must be initialized in the result object. If the semantics are lost before lowering, later codegen would naturally leave some fields uninitialized.

Potential secondary suspect because the bug concerns aggregate return-value construction. Named return value optimization can rewrite construction/copying of aggregate results, and a faulty optimization could cause the hidden result object to bypass initialization or to receive only partial stores.

Possible if scalar replacement of aggregates transforms the returned derived type so that only explicitly written fields are stored while untouched default-initialized fields are dropped, leading to exactly the observed garbage in some scalar members.

Aggregate return rewriting and remapping of returned-value variables happens here during generic tree transformations. Although less likely than gfortran frontend files, this is a plausible place where initialization of an aggregate return temporary could be lost.

The standard does allow unreachable cases, e.g. CASE (5:3). But they are a hassle for code generation, and to prevent that, we just cut them out here. We have the additional caveat that a SELECT construct could have been a computed GOTO in the source code. related_methods.reason: Most suspicious because the bug is specific to a function returning a derived type value. This routine is the main procedure-call lowering path and explicitly handles return parameters/results, so it is a likely place where a hidden function result temporary for a derived type could be created or passed back without applying default component initialization.

Highly suspicious because the failure pattern suggests only explicitly assigned constructor fields are copied while untouched components are left uninitialized instead of receiving type defaults. This method assigns a derived type constructor to a variable, which matches the suspected partial component-wise assignment path for function results.

This method explicitly creates or returns the decl used to hold a function return value. The bug is specific to derived-type function results not receiving default component initialization, so the hidden/fake result object is the most likely place where initialization requirements are being missed or the result storage is created without the normal local-variable initialization path.

Its documented role includes generating function entry code and performing initialization of deferred/local variables. A persistent difference between ordinary local declarations and function-result materialization strongly suggests the entry-time initialization machinery may initialize local derived-type objects correctly but omit the function result object, especially for default-initialized derived types.

This is the central translation routine for executable statements, making it the most suspicious place for mishandling function-result construction or assignment of derived-type results. The bug appears in the path where a function returns a derived type with default-initialized components, and this routine is broad enough to contain special handling that could bypass normal declaration-time initialization and emit only partial assignment into the result object.

This function drives code generation for a complete program unit after resolution, so it is a plausible place where function result variables are set up for procedures. Since local declarations are initialized correctly but function results are not, setup of the hidden result object during code generation is a strong candidate.

Most suspicious because the bug is specifically about missing default component initialization for a derived-type value produced through a function result. This method explicitly gets or generates a default initializer for a derived type, so if function-result construction reuses this machinery incorrectly or incompletely, some components could be left uninitialized.

Directly responsible for obtaining an expression for a default initializer of a derived type. A defect here could cause the returned object to lack the full default-initialization expression needed for untouched components, matching the observed garbage values in some fields.

Most directly tied to the failing path: the bug appears only when a derived type value is produced through a function result. This routine resolves function calls and determines the entity/type of the function result, so it is a prime place for mishandling result objects of derived type with default component initialization, especially if the result is not marked or prepared in the same way as an ordinary declared variable.

The report strongly suggests partial initialization of returned derived values, consistent with a structure-constructor or component-wise construction path that fills only explicitly provided components and omits applying default initializers to the rest. This method explicitly resolves structure constructors and initializers, making it highly suspicious for a bug where function-result construction bypasses full default initialization.

Core NRV transformation logic for aggregate returns. This pass rewrites returns of a local aggregate to construct directly into RESULT_DECL; a bug here could bypass or alter the normal initialization of the function result object, exactly matching a case where returned derived-type objects lose default-initialized component values.

This callback performs the actual tree rewriting of RETURN_EXPRs and replacements of the local return variable with RESULT_DECL. If this replacement is too aggressive or misses semantics attached to the original local variable, default initialization on the local aggregate could be lost, leaving some result fields uninitialized.

Most suspicious because the bug pattern is a partially initialized aggregate/function result, and this method explicitly rewrites assignments involving scalarized aggregates, generating subtree copies and replacements. A mistake here could copy only explicitly assigned components of a returned derived-type temporary while leaving default-initialized fields uninitialized, matching the observed garbage in some members after function return.

This routine generates the actual copying of scalar replacements into or out of an aggregate. If a function result aggregate is reconstructed from only touched scalar parts, untouched components with default initialization could be skipped, producing exactly the observed behavior of some fields retaining no valid initialization when materializing the returned object.

This method is the most suspicious because the bug is specifically about incorrect initialization of a function result object. Its documented role is to replace the callee RESULT_DECL with a dedicated return variable/slot during inlining, exactly the kind of transformation where default-initialized components of a returned aggregate could be lost if the created return object is not properly initialized before partial stores or copies.
